idea-plugin.name: ReDoS Catastrophic-Backtracking Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on a Pattern.compile("...")/ "...".matches("...") call in Java whose literal regex argument has a structural catastrophic-backtracking pattern: a nested unbounded quantifier ((a+)+), or an unbounded-quantified alternation with overlapping branches ((a|a)*). A single crafted input against either pattern can hang a server thread indefinitely (CWE-400, Uncontrolled Resource Consumption -- Regular Expression Denial of Service).

Parses the regex literal with its own hand-rolled grammar -- never depends on java.util.regex internally, since the platform exposes no PSI for the interior of a regex string. No plugin on the JetBrains Marketplace was found dedicated to this specific check.

Stated honestly: v0.1 covers Java only, only the two structural patterns named above -- not a full backtracking-cost engine -- and only a static string literal argument, never a regex built dynamically at runtime.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
